1-参考图尽量是人物全身正面照（本地int8模型跑的话），后期测试发现本地注意力不够，画面会乱
2-现目前是通用的提示词模板，我修改测试了好几个版本，但是不保证稳定性强！适合简单的动作迁移！最好的方式就是把白模的视频丢给agent，并说好一一对应的角色颜色去做H3的提示词，高动态的让agent去拆视频对帧去写！
3-通用模板的提示词抽卡率比较高，说到抽卡这个事，大家一定要有心理准备哈，别跑一两次觉得效果不行，就死犟！多抽抽卡呀，一张图片效果不好你还抽个十几二十次呢！

请分析我按输入顺序提供的 1–6 张角色参考图，生成用于替换 H3 通用模板中 {{CHARACTER_PROFILES}} 的英文角色描述。

这里的 Character 指目标角色，不限定为人类：真人、3D 玩偶、毛绒角色、卡通形象、拟人动物、机器人和吉祥物等均适用。按参考图判断角色类别，不把非人类角色默认描述成 woman、man 或 realistically proportioned human。

只输出实际提供角色的描述，不加解释，不输出未提供图片的占位条目。每张图应明确一个目标角色；若某张图含多个角色且未指定目标，请先问清目标，不擅自新增角色编号。

固定对应关系：
Character 1：<Picture 1>，对应视频蓝色 BLUE 源动作角色。
Character 2：<Picture 2>，对应视频红色 RED 源动作角色。
Character 3：<Picture 3>，对应视频绿色 GREEN 源动作角色。
Character 4：<Picture 4>，对应视频品红色 MAGENTA 源动作角色。
Character 5：<Picture 5>，对应视频青色 CYAN 源动作角色。
Character 6：<Picture 6>，对应视频黄色 YELLOW 源动作角色。

每个实际角色单独写一段英文，建议 80–140 个英文单词。按实际提供的图片，使用对应角色的完整英文段首：

Character 1 is the target character in <Picture 1>, assigned to the BLUE source performer.

Character 2 is the target character in <Picture 2>, assigned to the RED source performer.

Character 3 is the target character in <Picture 3>, assigned to the GREEN source performer.

Character 4 is the target character in <Picture 4>, assigned to the MAGENTA source performer.

Character 5 is the target character in <Picture 5>, assigned to the CYAN source performer.

Character 6 is the target character in <Picture 6>, assigned to the YELLOW source performer.

以上六句是对应角色的段首规则，不代表必须输出六个角色。只使用实际提供图片对应的句子，并在该句后继续写该角色的外观和比例描述；未提供的角色整段省略。

然后描述该角色图片里可见的固定设计：角色类别、视觉风格、身份特征、主体宽度相对高度、轮廓、各部分大小关系，以及实际具有的头部、躯干、四肢或其它结构的比例；补充材质、颜色、毛发、服装、鞋子及配饰等可见特征。没有的身体结构和服装不写，不为了凑字数编造人类的脸、手、脚或关节。

各角色分别描述，不平均体型。即使多张图的脸或外形相似，也保留每个角色独立的造型、材质及已有服饰。忠实保留 3D 玩偶或卡通角色的非标准比例、夸张结构和原始渲染风格，不默认写实，不改成人类标准体型。区分头部本体与耳朵、角、帽子等附属结构；区分衣服外轮廓与实际可见身体。无法看清的部位不要编造，不虚构精确比例数字，不把宽松服装解释为身体肥胖。

不描述参考图站姿、当前动作、镜头、背景或光线，不写剧情。不把蓝、红、绿、品红、青、黄这些动作标识颜色加入目标角色的身体表面、毛发、材质或衣服，除非参考图本身确实有该颜色。

Each entry links one image-defined target to one source performer. Preserve that target's own identity, physique, dimensions, proportions, materials and outfit. No character, category or setting is fixed by this template.
<Subject 2> is only each assigned performer's body action, facial expression and observable mouth state in <Video 1>, at the original times.
<Subject 3> is the actual environment behind the target in the selected picture, excluding the target and all alternate character views, close-up portraits, sheet panels and dividers. If no scene picture is designated, use only the non-character background regions of the first supplied picture, never its whole composition.
<Video 1> supplies performance only, not appearance, anatomy, body size, proportions, environment, lighting, composition or camera behaviour. Profile identifiers specify performance ownership only. Verified original audio, when supplied, provides a mouth-timing reference; soundtrack reuse requires a separate request.

summary:
[reference generation] Generate each role in <Subject 1> as its own moving character inside <Subject 3>, transferring only its assigned <Subject 2> performance. Preserve image-defined identities and proportions without copying reference-sheet layouts.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - retain each role's separate identity, body design, dimensions, proportions, style, materials and outfit as one distinct animated instance.
<Subject 2>: attribute_transfer - transfer only the assigned action, expression, gaze, visible mouth state, head coupling and timing.
<Subject 3>: fully_preserved - retain only actual environmental surfaces, existing scene objects, empty areas and lighting; exclude all character-reference views and page layout.
<Video 1>: fully_preserved - retain only its defined performance role, excluding all other source visual information.

detailed_description:
Generate one independently animated instance of every configured role in one shared scene. Static portraits, printed figures and back-view panels do not count as role performances. Each role participates as its own moving character; never duplicate it to fill another role's motion stream.
[Shot 1] Begin directly in each assigned source action phase, expression and readable mouth state, adapted to the correct target's unchanged design. Do not start from the reference pose or introduce preparation movement.

Character images define identities, not background plates. Multiple views of one individual describe one role, not extra people or decoration. Reconstruct one coherent moving character from them. Exclude all such heads, body views, repeats and panel separators from the background. Do not display the original reference image behind the performers.

Build <Subject 3> only from the picture's actual non-character environment. Preserve shown surfaces, existing objects, lighting and visual treatment. When only a plain backing surface is shown, retain that surface and its empty areas without adding scenery or decoration. When a real scene is shown, retain its recognizable environment without treating the target character as part of the background. Use one shared environment, not a collage. Character clothing, identity, era or story does not determine the setting. Do not import the motion video's environment or camera.

Preserve each target's facial identity, physique, width-to-height and head-to-body ratios, torso, limb lengths and thicknesses, and hand or foot sizes where present. Retain original dimensions and image-based scene-scale cues. Do not resize or reshape it to match a source, average physiques or equalize heights. Retain its own anatomical category and expressive structures without adding missing human anatomy.

Frame the complete movement range from the beginning, keeping heads, appendages, reaching limbs, feet, hems and accessories visible except for requested exits. Gain room through a wider view or staging, not deformation, independent resizing or cropping side performers. Perspective may change projected size while body dimensions stay stable. Source zooms, cuts, cropping and screen sizes are not target camera or scale instructions.

Reconstruct the entire visible target, including existing body parts, surfaces, outfit and accessories, from its own image. Leave no source mannequin, leftover limbs or target-head/source-body mixture. Source markings have no appearance role.

Keep assignments through turns, crossings, occlusions and source position changes. Never exchange identities, outfits, expressions or body parts, or clone a target for an unassigned source. Retarget joint motion, orientation, coordination, support, locomotion and interaction timing to the target's own structure and scene placement. Match actions rather than source screen coordinates, skeleton dimensions or outlines. Keep bodies distinct during contact.

Follow only observed facial changes in brows, eyelids, blinking, gaze, cheeks, lips, jaw and head, including intensity, asymmetry, holds and release. Preserve identity and keep unchanged regions still. Body movement alone does not imply speech, laughter, gasping or an open jaw.

Copy the assigned source's visible mouth state at corresponding times: closed, slightly parted, open or still. Preserve closure for its full observed interval and retain small resting gaps without enlarging them. Match upper- and lower-lip contours, corners, jaw, holds and head coupling on the target's own face. Show teeth or tongue only when supported by source evidence and target anatomy.
